fieldMarks: Large all-white swan, 3 ft 11 in-4 ft 7 in.
Black bill (not orange as in Mute Swan), usually with a small yellow spot in front of the eye.
Juveniles dull gray-brown with a pinkish bill, whitening by midwinter.
Call a mellow, bugling 'hoo-ho-hoo', often heard from migrating flocks.
behavior: Migrating flocks of up to 100 or more are made up of family groups; fall migration uses long flights between traditional staging areas.
Dabbles, dips or up-ends in water for aquatic plants; on migration and in winter feeds heavily on waste corn, barley and soybeans in fields, sometimes on moonlit nights.
habitat: Breeds on northern tundra with many lakes and ponds, usually near the coast.
Winters on shallow lakes, wide slow rivers and coastal estuaries, especially near farm fields.
range: Breeds on Arctic tundra of Alaska and northern Canada and migrates long distances to winter on both coasts and interior waters of the United States.

lookalikes.name: Mute swan
lookalikes.howToTell: Mute swan has an orange bill; adult tundra swan's bill is black, usually with a small yellow spot before the eye.
